answer: Agent identities wander across a transaction graph, so anomaly detection scores each new node by its subgraph's degree and neighbor overlap against known honest clusters. A sybil ring's accounts show a pearl of near-identical timing and shared counterparties, flagged when the tight component's internal edge density exceeds a threshold. That forces attackers to fake diverse histories across a wide canyon of unrelated wallets, raising cost per identity superlinearly; the limit is slow-drip sybils mimicking organic growth.
